measured_on: Linux cloud container, 4 vCPUs (Intel Xeon 2.80 GHz, AVX2, no SHA extensions); software, not robot hardware
method: median of 3 runs; before = commit caaf645 built in a separate worktree, after = this change; same machine, same session

station_ingest_records_per_s.note: cargo run --release -p cursiv-evidence --example bench -- 5000 3 with CURSIV_BENCH_BATCH=<n>; store API, no HTTP

end_to_end_sync_records_per_s.note: 15,000 pre-signed records from a cursiv_ros2 StreamingAgent outbox to a cursiv-bridge on loopback (HTTP), sync(batch=<n>)

wire_size.note: 84 records of the committed sample package; compression is used automatically when the station is not on loopback

rejected_change: HTTP keep-alive in the Python client made batch-100 sync 3.9x slower (6,851 -> 1,760 records/s): tiny_http writes response headers and body separately without TCP_NODELAY, so each reused-connection request waited ~40 ms for a delayed ACK. One connection per request is kept.
